definitionBean.title: Tangent to a Circle
definitionBean.definition: A line that touches a circle at exactly one point is called a tangent.
definitionBean.explanation: A tangent touches the circle at only one point, called the point of contact. The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent, forming an angle of 90°.
importantPoints: A tangent touches a circle at only one point
The radius at the point of contact makes an angle of 90°
Only one tangent can be drawn to a circle from a point on it
Tangents and radii are perpendicular to each other

parts.statement: From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and the distance of Q from the center is 25 cm. Find the radius of the circle.
parts.explanation:
Given:
Tangent length (PQ) = 24 cm
Distance from the center (OQ) = 25 cm

We know that the radius of a circle is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact. Therefore, triangle OPQ is a right-angled triangle with ∠OPQ = 90°.

Using the Pythagorean theorem:
OQ² = OP² + PQ²
(25)² = OP² + (24)²
625 = OP² + 576
OP² = 625 - 576
OP² = 49
OP = 7 cm

Therefore, the radius of the circle is 7 cm.

parts.statement: If TP and TQ are two tangents to a circle with center O such that ∠POQ = 110°, then find ∠PTQ.
parts.explanation:
Given:
∠POQ = 110°

In quadrilateral OPTQ (where P and Q are points of contact), the radii OP and OQ are perpendicular to the tangents TP and TQ respectively.
Therefore, ∠OPT = 90° and ∠OQT = 90°.

The sum of all angles in a quadrilateral is 360°:
∠PTQ + ∠OPT + ∠OQT + ∠POQ = 360°
∠PTQ + 90° + 90° + 110° = 360°
∠PTQ + 290° = 360°
∠PTQ = 360° - 290°
∠PTQ = 70°
